html:
Binding review, approval and mapped-call flows

A successful call can supply evidence for a reusable parameter mapping. A person reviews the recorded sources and destinations, previews a proposal, then explicitly approves it. Approval saves a rule for newly accepted tasks; it does not pause, resume, steer or retry the task being reviewed. The model still chooses future calls, and native admission decides whether an approved rule applies.

The Parameters manual explains the user flow. Parameter storage and bindings owns ordinary reference capture and exact field injection. The separate correction editor can explicitly request Pause and prepare an Agent-owned retry; those actions are not part of this save-only review surface.

Correction-session and learned-workflow flows trace explicit Pause ownership, frozen Apply recovery, ordered teaching and fresh current-run dependencies.

Owners and data

flowchart TD Accepted[Invocation accepted parameter snapshot] --> Review[BindingReviews evidence reconstruction] Receipt[Exact successful invocation receipt] --> Review Contract[Current tool contract and recorded provenance] --> Review Review --> UI[Masked browser review and explicit choices] UI --> Preview[Stateless server preview and token] Preview --> Approve[Explicit approval and revalidation] Approve --> Transaction[One authority transaction] Transaction --> Rule[Reusable rule and immutable history] Transaction --> Generation[Approval generation and evidence receipt] Generation --> NewTask[New task captures current generation] Rule --> Admission[Native mapped-call preparation] NewTask --> Admission Proposal[Model-selected tool call] --> Admission Admission --> Pinned[Resolved arguments and private execution inputs] Pinned --> Execution[Existing native admission and execution owners] Execution --> Use[Application outcome record] Human[Explicit user result assessment] --> Use Use --> Suspension[Incorrect verdict can suspend the used revision] Suspension --> Admission
Owner Responsibility and boundary
parameter_binding_reviews.js Run-owned inline rows, local drafts, masked preview, explicit approval and refresh. Shared parameter_mapping.js components supply field controls and HTTP calls.
Review routes Strict request shapes and pagination bounds; delegate to BindingReviews. Application middleware owns authentication. Review conflicts become HTTP 409.
BindingReviews Verify ownership, reconstruct exact evidence, project public data, validate edited intent and re-preview before approval.
binding_approvals and MappingStore Current documents, immutable revisions, idempotency, approval generation and evidence. Use Controller RAM authority or standalone SQLite according to the Parameter Store owner.
mappings and ssh_mapping Source identity/type checks, destination templates, structural matching and deterministic materialization. They return arguments and private environment; they do not execute commands.
native/learned_mappings.py Filter rules at admission, pin resolved inputs, claim required explicit selections and record later execution outcomes.

Execution success, approval of a reusable mapping and the user's judgment that a result was correct are separate fields. Public review data masks all argument scalars and lists source identities/pointers. Approval evidence stores identities, revisions, recorded/approved bindings and the preview token, rather than copying accepted parameter values. Reusable templates retain unmapped argument structure; the existing template check rejects known protected values and credential literals.

Discover and reconstruct recorded evidence

sequenceDiagram actor Human participant UI as Run footer and stable rows participant API as Review API and service participant Runs as Native run and receipt store participant Rules as Mapping documents Human->>UI: Open Parameter bindings UI->>API: GET candidates for request and run API->>Runs: Verify ownership and accepted bound mode API->>Runs: Read scalar invocation metadata newest first loop Until eligible page is full or metadata ends API->>Runs: Read invocation and its exact settled receipt API->>Rules: Read prior learned revision when recorded API->>API: Verify complete success, contract and source provenance end API-->>UI: Masked candidates, unavailable count and order cursor UI->>UI: Insert new rows or refresh existing metadata Human->>UI: Expand one Review binding row UI->>API: GET detailed invocation review API->>API: Reconstruct evidence again API-->>UI: Source IDs, destinations, masked original and revisions UI->>UI: Retain this mounted editor through later list refreshes

The service accepts only a run owned by the supplied request and captured in bound mode. The receipt must be executed, successful, explicitly complete and available; shell/Python process reviews additionally require a recorded zero exit code. Artifact lookup is confined to that invocation's run. Missing history or a changed tool contract makes the evidence unavailable.

For an ordinary recorded field binding, the service reconstructs the accepted parameter identity, revision and pointer, then verifies the exact destination value and type. This verifies an already-recorded relationship. It does not discover a relationship by searching for equal values. Automatic code-input injection and Agent narration do not establish a reviewable field mapping.

binding_evidence.concrete projects supported activity, sequence and parallel provenance onto an individual child. It strips the child's pointer prefix and retains supported sequence-wide fields. Unsupported or absent child relationships remain unavailable. Previously learned invocations use their pinned rule history and source revisions. Prior-result mappings can be displayed but are managed in the mapping library rather than edited through this parameter-only review form.

Pagination uses invocation order, including skipped unavailable rows. New calls do not shift an existing cursor. The browser refreshes metadata through the oldest mounted row, preserves expanded editors and restores the focused/visible anchor's scroll position. Closing hides the panel; it neither cancels a request nor changes task state. Detached/hidden panels discard returned list presentation updates.

Preview, explicit approval and atomic persistence

sequenceDiagram actor Human participant UI as Local review draft participant Service as BindingReviews participant Queue as Task-queue lock participant Authority as RAM or SQLite mapping authority participant Updates as UI update broker Human->>UI: Select sources and destinations, then preview UI->>Service: Proposal plus observed and saved revisions Service->>Service: Reconstruct accepted evidence and validate edited rule Service-->>UI: Masked preview, edited flag and exact token Human->>UI: Approve and save for future tasks UI->>Service: Same intent, token and idempotency key Service->>Authority: Look for prior approval identity alt Exact idempotent retry Authority-->>Service: Prior approval with matching request hash Service-->>UI: Same receipt without a new generation else New approval intent Service->>Queue: Acquire lock Service->>Service: Re-preview and compare token Service->>Authority: Atomically recheck revision and commit Note over Authority: Reuse equivalent rule, or create rule and advance generation Note over Authority: Persist approval evidence and current/history rows together Authority-->>Service: Committed approval receipt Service->>Queue: Release lock Service->>Updates: Publish parameters.changed Service-->>UI: Saved rule identity and generation end UI->>UI: Lock saved draft and expose mapping-library action

Each draft identifies its request/run/invocation, observed evidence digest, expected saved revision and explicit source IDs. The server resolves those IDs only against the invocation's accepted catalog. It does not refresh the task from today's saved parameter values. Preview materializes and schema-checks the proposal, checks the template and hashes the evidence, rule, resolved source revisions and expected revision into a token. Changing choices requires another preview. An edited proposal is labeled unexecuted even though the original call succeeded.

Approval repeats preview while holding the task-queue lock. The persistence transaction also rechecks the reviewed saved revision, protecting the interval between preview and commit. Controller RAM uses records.atomic; standalone SQLite uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE. A new reusable rule advances the generation once. An equivalent reusable rule is reused; its title, enabled state and descriptive metadata are not part of equivalence, and reuse does not re-enable a disabled rule.

The authority writes the rule/generation when needed and the separate approval evidence receipt with immutable history. A reused idempotency key with different request content is a conflict. Stale evidence, edited templates or incompatible source/contract data require inspection/preview again. Ordinary storage exceptions propagate; the approval transaction does not partially publish its records.

Which tasks can use an approval

flowchart TD Save[Approve a new reusable rule] --> G[Rule receives generation G] Accept[Accept a new bound task] --> Capture[Capture current approval generation] Capture --> Snapshot[Persist task parameter snapshot] Old[Already accepted, queued or continued task] --> Keep[Retain its earlier generation] Edit[Edit or merge accepted inputs] --> Keep Keep --> Snapshot G --> Check{Rule generation at or below task boundary?} Snapshot --> Check Check -->|No| Exclude[Exclude ordinary future-use review rule] Check -->|Yes| Eligible[Consider scope, source identity and structural match] Occurrence[Create a later scheduled occurrence] --> Accept Correction[Separate explicit correction selection] --> Selected[Use its own revisioned selection and claim rules]

resolve_references captures the authority generation for a new bound snapshot. When a previous snapshot exists it preserves that generation; absent legacy watermarks mean zero. Input merges and task revision helpers preserve the original boundary too. Queue waiting, restart and Continue do not acquire later approvals. Each newly created scheduled occurrence performs its own acceptance.

Native preparation and model-facing mapping hints filter review rules against this boundary. Legacy correction rules have generation zero. An explicit selection from the separate correction flow has its own admission/claim semantics; the save-only review API creates neither a correction session nor that selection. Generation eligibility alone does not authorize an execution: scope, identity, contract, enablement, suspension and tool admission still apply.

Materialize a future call and record its outcome

sequenceDiagram participant Model as Agent model participant Native as Native preparation participant Library as Mapping store participant Inputs as Accepted sources participant Execute as Execution owner participant Use as Outcome records Model->>Native: Propose a tool call Native->>Library: Read eligible rules and<br/>explicit selection if present Native->>Native: Check generation, scope, match<br/>and workflow dependencies alt Ambiguous, suspended or changed contract Native-->>Model: Mapping rejection without a guessed connection else One eligible rule Native->>Inputs: Resolve exact identities,<br/>pointers and types Inputs-->>Native: Values and source revisions Native->>Native: Materialize arguments and schema-check Native->>Execute: Pin revision, inputs<br/>and private environment Execute->>Library: Claim required<br/>selection revision once Execute->>Execute: Apply ordinary admission and execution rules Execute->>Use: Record execution or settlement outcome Note over Use: Preserve independent<br/>user correctness feedback end

Generic rules match the reviewed argument skeleton and replace only named destinations. Runtime routing/internal fields and inputs.parameters are excluded. Source identity includes the parameter's creation identity, so deleting and recreating the same key does not silently reuse the old approval. Materialization uses the task's accepted value/revision and rejects missing pointers or changed types. Result sources require one successful current-run producer; old output is not reused as fresh input, and learned workflow consumers wait for their dependencies.

The SSH adapter recognizes bounded literal commands and connection roles. It rejects unsupported local-shell expansion/compound syntax instead of interpreting it. Connection matching uses reviewed identity or an explicit rule alias, excludes password and remote-command text from that selector, and never guesses between multiple servers. Rendering preserves the remote program and unrelated options, validates connection values, and returns passwords through private SSHPASS with sshpass -e. Native preparation pins that environment beside the accepted call; public mapping projections expose rule/source revisions only.

An accepted selection revision can be claimed once for a required explicit choice; an identical operation replay is idempotent. Later library edits cannot rewrite the already materialized invocation. Ordinary unmatched calls retain their existing path, while an unresolved symbolic mapping host is rejected. Other permissions, approvals, Gateway checks and dispatch ownership remain with the existing engine.

Outcome observation stores execution status, exit code and pending/settled state separately from user feedback. It retries limited revision conflicts to retain a concurrent assessment and ignores terminal-to-pending regressions. Reporting an incorrect mapping records suspension of the used revision and can disable an equivalent current rule. Feedback, suspension and disablement are successive repository writes, unlike the single atomic approval transaction. Network or process failure alone does not suspend a learned mapping.

Implementation and validation map

  • Browser review owner and review routes.
  • Evidence reconstruction, composite provenance, approval transaction and versioned mapping store.
  • Matching/materialization, SSH adapter, native admission and outcome hooks, reference capture and existing correction owner.
  • Review evidence/concurrency fixtures, activation and recovery fixtures, mapping/store fixtures and inline browser fixtures.

These fixtures distinguish software behavior from autonomous model reliability. The retained November 4 acceptance report records its own isolated live-execution scope and limitations. Its measurements are historical evidence, not new runs performed for this documentation review.
